intro: For about sixty years, no Black player took the field in major league baseball. No rule book said so. Owners kept the line by habit and agreement from the late 1880s until April 15, 1947. In those years Black players and owners built leagues of their own, with constitutions, standings and a championship.

Other doors were locked by written rules. English rowing barred manual workers as amateurs. The Olympics barred paid athletes for most of a century. The PGA wrote a whites-only clause in 1934. Women waited decades for events of their own.

In this unit you will read rules, votes, letters and records. You will match each rule to the people it shut out and the date the door opened. You will be able to explain how written and unwritten rules both worked, and who changed them.
bigQuestion: Who wrote the rules that kept people out of sport, and how were those doors opened?

timeline.t: Baseball's national association votes to keep out clubs with Black members
Henley Royal Regatta bars manual workers from amateur rowing
Moses Fleetwood Walker plays in the major leagues for Toledo
International League votes to sign no new Black players
Paris congress founds the IOC and makes the Games amateur
Women compete at the Olympics for the first time
Jim Thorpe loses his 1912 Olympic medals
Rube Foster founds the Negro National League
Jackie Robinson and Larry Doby cross the major league color line
The PGA repeals its whites-only clause
The IOC drops the word amateur; Little League opens to girls
MLB recognizes seven Negro Leagues as major leagues

test.q: What was the major league color line?
choices: An unwritten agreement to keep Black players off rosters
A clause in the Official Baseball Rules
test.why: No major league rule barred Black players; owners kept an unwritten agreement.

test.q: Which player was in the major leagues in 1884?
test.why: Walker caught for Toledo of the American Association, a major league, in 1884.

test.q: What did the International League decide in July 1887?
choices: To approve no new contracts with Black players
test.why: Its directors voted on July 14, 1887, to sign no new Black players.

test.q: Where did Rube Foster and other owners found the Negro National League?
choices: The Paseo YMCA in Kansas City
test.why: The league was founded at the Paseo YMCA in Kansas City in February 1920.

test.q: Which Chicago event was a highlight of the Black baseball year?
choices: The East-West All-Star Game at Comiskey Park
test.why: The East-West All-Star Game began at Comiskey Park in 1933 and drew huge crowds.

test.q: Who crossed the American League color line in July 1947?
test.why: Larry Doby joined Cleveland on July 5, 1947.

test.q: Who was the first woman elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame?
test.why: Newark Eagles co-owner Effa Manley was elected in 2006.

test.q: What did the Henley mechanics clause do?
choices: Barred manual workers from amateur rowing
test.why: The 1879 Henley definition barred mechanics, artisans and laborers.

test.q: Why was John B. Kelly's 1920 Henley entry important?
choices: He was refused, then won Olympic gold that summer
test.why: Henley refused Kelly, and he won two Olympic golds at Antwerp in 1920.

test.q: What happened to Jim Thorpe's medals in 2022?
choices: He was named sole champion of both events
They were given to another athlete
test.why: In July 2022 the IOC recognized Thorpe as the sole champion of the pentathlon and decathlon.

test.q: What did the IOC change in 1974?
choices: It dropped the word amateur from its eligibility rule
test.why: The 1974 Olympic Charter eligibility rule no longer required athletes to be amateurs.

test.q: How did the PGA's color line differ from the NFL's?
choices: The NFL's was written and the PGA's was not
The PGA's was a written clause from 1934 to 1961
test.why: The PGA wrote a whites-only clause into its constitution; the NFL's 1934 to 1945 ban was unwritten.

test.q: What did Black tennis players found in 1916?
choices: The United States Lawn Tennis Association
test.why: The ATA was founded in 1916 because top events were at clubs that shut Black players out.

test.q: When were women first allowed to run the Boston Marathon officially?
test.why: Boston officially opened to women in 1972.

test.q: What did Major League Baseball do in December 2020?
choices: Recognized seven Negro Leagues from 1920 to 1948 as major leagues
Removed Josh Gibson from the Hall of Fame
test.why: MLB recognized seven Negro Leagues as major leagues in December 2020.

write.prompt: Which kind of barrier was harder to remove: a written rule or an unwritten one? Use two or three records from this unit, such as the 1887 International League vote, the 1879 Henley definition, the PGA clause of 1934 to 1961, or the Olympic Charter change of 1974. Name each record and its date, say who made it and who it shut out, and explain how and when the door opened.
tips: Name each rule or record and give its year.
Say who made the rule and who it kept out.
Explain what changed it: a vote, a lawsuit, a public lease or a person's action.
Compare the barriers rather than only listing them.
Use unit words such as color line, clause and eligibility.
